title: Anton Philips Came for Six Months to Sell His Brother's Lamps
conflicts: 1895 production: Heerding (Biografisch Woordenboek van Nederland) says 400,000 lamps rising to 4 million a year by 1905; Dirk van Delft (Inventing Europe) says a twentyfold rise to 4 million, implying about 200,000, matching a Dutch local history (200,000 in 1895). The story gives only the agreed 1905 figure. Timing: van Delft says Philips profited from 1894, while the International Directory of Company Histories puts the decision to sell in 1894 after 1893 losses; the story says trial production had ended by late 1894 but the firm still lacked a seller. The 1894 sale attempt is single-sourced (IDCH, reproduced on several sites) and is attributed in the text.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'mixed' to 'bootstrapped': the firm was financed by co-founder Frederik Philips and no outside investors were found. Anton arrived in early January 1895 per the Philips Company Archives. Quote stance: affirms.
